claims.source: WikiLeaks, The Podesta Emails, corpus search, https://wikileaks.org/podesta-emails/?q=prometheus and https://wikileaks.org/podesta-emails/?q=moulton
claims.text: Neither Prometheus nor Linda Moulton Howe appears in the release. A search of the WikiLeaks Podesta Emails interface for 'prometheus' returns five emails, all of them American Bar Association technology transfer law circulars addressed to podesta@LAW.GEORGETOWN.EDU, and a search for 'moulton' returns sixteen, none of them hers and none from DeLonge. Thirteen emails in the release were sent from t.delonge@me.com and none of them is among either set.

On Debriefed, episode 82, 3 April 2026, Michael Phillip said the Prometheus and Greek mythology framing reached him through 'the conversations between Podesta and McCaslin and dalong and then by way of dalong lavenda' in the WikiLeaks release, while stating in the same passage that 'I don't know verbatim what he actually said. I'm sort of regurgitating this from talking to lavenda.' The release contains the correspondence he names and does not contain the content he attributes to it.

desc: On 25 January 2016 Tom DeLonge emailed John Podesta under the subject line 'General McCasland'. The email disputes a description of the general as a sceptic, says DeLonge had been working with him for four months and had given him a four hour presentation on the project, asserts that the Roswell material was shipped to the laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and that General McCasland had been in charge of that laboratory until a couple of years earlier, and says the general helped assemble DeLonge's advisory team. dossier.narrative: The Podesta release is an instrument as much as a document set: raw headers, message ids and reply chains, which is why claims taken off it can be checked rather than believed. This email is the strongest single item in it for this board, because DeLonge disputes the characterisation of the general as a sceptic, says he had been working with him for four months and had given him a four hour presentation, and asserts that the Roswell material was shipped to the laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and that the general had been in charge of that laboratory until a couple of years earlier. The calendar thread shows the general was a party to the correspondence and not merely its subject. The corpus opened here adds a second named correspondent inside the same release, read the same way: Bob Fish, writing to Podesta over three days in March 2015, naming the Defense Support Program as a collector of hard data on unidentified flying objects and saying in the same email that he was never fully briefed into that operation directly. The two together are what the release is for on this board: private assertions by identifiable people, dated, with the qualifications the popular retelling drops.
openQuestions: Whether any government record corroborates the assertion about Wright-Patterson custody; none opened for this node does.
The general's own account of the four hour presentation.
dossier.whatItIs: An email of 25 January 2016 from Tom DeLonge to John Podesta under the subject line 'General McCasland', published by WikiLeaks in the Podesta Emails on 10 October 2016 as email id 3099, together with the calendar thread of the same days in which the general is himself a correspondent.
dossier.whyImplicated: It is one of the few documents on this board in which a named general officer is placed, in contemporaneous private correspondence rather than in testimony, inside a conversation about Roswell material and the laboratory at Wright-Patterson. It is a primary record of what was said, not of what is true, and the board carries it on that footing.
